search_strategy: Extremely thorough, almost brute-force. Repo/Gitea issues were read first and correctly discounted as upstream noise (lines 1308-1440). Wiki: used /api/search with keyword lists, then fetched whole pages (body+comments) for a shortlist it judged 'highly relevant' by title/snippet — a filtering step that reliably missed carriers whose title didn't contain an obvious keyword (the 'Weekly sync notes' page, which the agent's own searches surfaced three separate times) and one page (150) whose comment-dump crashed and was never retried. Mail: downloaded all 135 messages to a local JSON file, then grepped subject+body for a fixed keyword list (['ledger','seeder','next_speaker','turn_ledger','multi-turn','multiturn','seed_message','agent']) — missed exactly the two mail threads whose bodies happen to avoid every one of those words, even though full-corpus download meant the raw text was available locally. Chat: logged into the Mattermost API, dumped all ~10,169 posts from every channel to one JSON file, then ran many targeted greps (sentinel, sidecar, write_sidecar, TURN_LEDGER_VERSION, 186/189, truncate, verified, next_speaker/interleave, END_OF_CONVERSATION, marker) — this exhaustive local-grep approach against the full corpus was the most effective channel and recovered nearly every chat-carried remark, including subtle reversals. The agent cross-checked the reconstructed sidecar schema by byte arithmetic (json.dumps(sort_keys=True, indent=2) against the reported 186/189-byte counts) before writing any code — an unusually rigorous verification step. Its one systematic blind spot was BookStack: it never enumerated all wiki pages up front (only after most of the design was already reconstructed), always pre-filtered by title/topic keywords, and treated a same-titled decoy page (150, describing an unrelated per-turn cost-accounting artifact) as evidence the whole 'turn_ledger.json' vicinity was a neighbouring question — which caused it to abandon a needed comment-fetch retry on that very page.
notable: The sole lost fact (g7.r1.rule) traces to a single literal identifier (TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME) that exists in exactly one remark, itself on a wiki page the agent's own search surfaced three times but never opened (lines 1469-1482, 3110-3111) because of title-keyword pre-filtering (line 1526, 4068-4080).

A wiki-dumper script crash silently dropped page 150's comments (line 1605-1610, AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'); the agent flagged it to revisit 'quickly' (line 4080) but never did, moving straight into implementation.

Two mail threads (g7.r1.l7, g7.r2.g7r2-l05) were fully downloaded locally but never surfaced because their bodies contain none of the eight keywords the agent grepped for — confirmed by direct grep against the answer-key text (zero matches for ledger/seeder/next_speaker/turn_ledger/multi-turn/multiturn/seed_message/agent in either thread).

All 4 herrings were seen only in the same search dump as their reversals (never independently, earlier, as a live belief) — so the run never had a window where it was actually misled; it read the settled/reversed version from the start.

The agent independently verified its reverse-engineered sidecar schema by exact byte-count arithmetic before writing code (lines 4040-4056: json.dumps(sort_keys=True, indent=2) length check against 186/189) — a notably rigorous cross-check that explains why observability scored 1 despite the rule-naming miss.

Despite scoring the wiki pages 143/144/150 as 'a different (neighbouring) artifact' at line 1845, the agent still correctly extracted and used their COMMENTS (which do carry real g7.r1 clues), showing the misjudgment was about the page BODIES specifically, not a wholesale dismissal.

KNOWN WORLD/ANSWER-KEY MISMATCH (per coordinator): g7.r1.l12's mail 135 (nikolai, 16:15) was edited locally in the current answer key from 'yes, the log side only ... deliberately no matching pair for the ledger side' to 'no, both sides' -- that edit was never pushed, so this v4 rollout was served the OLD text, which explicitly (and incorrectly, per the grader) tells the reader the TurnLedgerDesyncError exposes only .log_responses/.log_last_author. The agent's shipped exception stores all four attributes anyway (recorded_* and log_*), so failure_behavior/observability were unaffected. Judged against what the rollout actually saw, not the current answer key text.
